channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Anthropic IPO Is Fairly Priced, Says Dharmesh Thakker
item.description: The expected Anthropic IPO shows that artificial intelligence demand is real, says Battery Ventures General Partner Dharmesh Thakker. He says the IPO is fairly priced on "Bloomberg Deals." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fortress’s Burton: Investors More Discerning on AI
item.description: Stocks fell as Nvidia’s post-earnings rally sputtered, with Anthropic on the cusp of a potentially record-breaking IPO. Fortress Chief Strategist Elizabeth Burton says investors are becoming more discerning about the AI trade, focusing more on fundamentals as they pick through the winners and losers. She spoke on Bloomberg Open Interest. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Recent Tech Outages, Disruptions Not Related, US Says
item.description: Leaders from DHS and the FBI said Wednesday there was “no indication” that the spate of recent tech outages and disruptions were related or the result of terrorism. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia Moves On From Huang as Anthropic IPO Looms
item.description: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down Nvidia's earnings report, with the AI chip giant reassuring investors that Jensen Huang isn't coming back, and that Nvidia will do just fine without him. Plus, all eyes on Anthropic as the AI company is tracking to price its shares above the marketed range in its IPO, and Grand Theft Auto VI becomes the best-reviewed game of all time ahead of its release tomorrow. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: GTA VI Becomes Best-Reviewed Video Game Ever
item.description: Grand Theft Auto VI, the highly-anticipated game one decade in the making, has become the best-reviewed game of all time ahead of its release. Bloomberg video game reporter Cecilia D'Anastasio joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic’s VC Backers Double Down Ahead of IPO
item.description: Some of Anthropic’s biggest existing venture investors are looking to put even more money into its blockbuster IPO, an unusual move as competition for shares intensifies. Bloomberg’s Natasha Mascarenhas joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia Earnings Impress, But Succession Risk Lingers
item.description: Nvidia beat expectations and raised its growth outlook, but questions remain over life after Jensen Huang. KeyBanc Capital Markets Managing Director John Vinh discusses the CEO search, talent risks and Nvidia’s push to secure more AI chip capacity with Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apollo Sees Huge Europe Finance Demand for AI, Defense
item.description: Apollo sees a major opportunity to provide long-term capital in Europe, where fragmented markets are fueling direct lending growth. The firm, which is launching a €10 billion regional private-credit arm, is particularly focused on financing defense supply chains as Europe’s investment needs rise. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic IPO Demand Sets Stage for Historic Debut
item.description: Anthropic is expected to price its blockbuster IPO at or above the top of its marketed range, after the offering drew orders for multiple times the shares available. Bloomberg’s Bailey Lipschultz and Bloomberg Intelligence’s Christopher Cain break down what could become the largest IPO fundraising ever and why history suggests getting shares at the IPO price can make a major difference to investor returns. They join Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic Takes Center Stage After Nvidia
item.description: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Nvidia says it can keep winning without Jensen Huang, but one analyst tells us the board may have moved too fast. Meanwhile, Anthropic prepares for a blockbuster IPO as Blackstone’s Viral Patel says the AI investment boom is only accelerating. Plus, Bloomberg Opinion Columnist Jonathan Levin on the battle over China’s access to American technology. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Thoma Bravo’s Proofpoint Cuts Costs on $2 Billion Debt Deal
item.description: Thoma Bravo-backed Proofpoint Inc. is cutting its borrowing costs and nixing a discount to investors on a near $2 billion debt sale, as lenders pile into the deal, according to people familiar with the transaction.
item.dc:creator: Aaron Weinman, Gowri Gurumurthy and Jeannine Amodeo

item.title: Nvidia Argues to Wary Investors That It Can Thrive Without Huang
item.description: Nvidia Corp. sought to deliver a clear message during its first earnings update since the departure of longtime leader Jensen Huang: He’s not coming back, and the company will be fine without him. Dan Ives, Partner at Yorkville Ives & Co., breaks down Nvidia earnings, Collette Kress' debut, and the future of Nvidia. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Viral Patel on AI’s Investment Boom
item.description: Viral Patel. the CEO of Blackstone’s private equity fund BXPE says AI demand is accelerating, not slowing, as companies ramp up adoption. He sees the biggest investment opportunity in AI infrastructure and computing, where supply may lag demand for years. Patel also points to private-market exits, selective investing, and opportunities beyond AI. Blackstone is a large investor in Anthropic. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic IPO: CFO Krishna Rao Helps Grow Startup Into AI Powerhouse
item.description: Near the start of the year, a rift was quickly widening between the US government and Anthropic PBC over safe use of artificial intelligence. The Pentagon was pushing Anthropic to loosen restrictions on how its tools are used in combat, and threatened to cancel a contract worth hundreds of millions of dollars. item.dc:creator: Shirin Ghaffary and Natasha Mascarenhas

item.title: Helsing Pulls Back From Plymouth UK Project After Losing Out on Navy Contract
item.description: Helsing, Europe’s most valuable defense startup, is retreating from its flagship project in the UK to manufacture underwater naval drones a year after unveiling the plan with political fanfare, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Mark Bergen and Christina Kyriasoglou

item.title: Higher Rates to Push Firms to Private Credit as Stress Rises
item.description: Rising interest rates are set to impede access to public markets for more borrowers, prompting them to seek funds from private credit lenders instead.
item.dc:creator: Tasos Vossos and Tolu M Alamutu

item.title: The Bank of Nvidia Is Getting More ‘Disciplined,’ Selective
item.description: The Bank of Nvidia — which AI startups, computing providers and model developers around the world have come to depend on for multibillion-dollar investments and financial backstops — is becoming more discriminating.
item.dc:creator: Dina Bass and Ian King

item.title: Senate Hearing Condemns Roblox’s Child Safety Record
item.description: An 11-year-old boy was tricked into sending explicit photos of himself to a man he met on the gaming platform Roblox. The stranger threatened to share the images with members of an online gaming group, and the boy begged him to delete the photos. Later, the boy confronted the man at his home in Venus, Texas, where he was sexually assaulted.
item.dc:creator: Cecilia D'Anastasio

item.description: Nvidia Corp. sought to deliver a clear message during its first earnings update since the departure of longtime leader Jensen Huang: He’s not coming back, and the company will be fine without him.

item.title: Why GTA VI Took 13 Years and $1 Billion to Make
item.description: Grand Theft Auto VI is expected to be one of the biggest entertainment releases in history, and potentially one of the most expensive. Why is there so much riding on the game? (Source: Bloomberg)
